words.definition: sure about your ability; not afraid

sentences.sentence: She feels confident about her English exam.
He spoke in a confident voice during the meeting.
Do you feel confident about your presentation?

words.definition: worried and a little afraid about something

sentences.sentence: He was nervous before his job interview.
I always feel nervous when I speak in public.
Are you still nervous about flying?

words.definition: you can trust this person or thing to work well

sentences.sentence: Tom is a reliable friend who always helps me.
We need a reliable internet connection for work.
Is your laptop reliable enough for travel?

words.definition: not wanting to work or move much

sentences.sentence: I was too lazy to cook, so we ordered pizza.
He is not lazy, he just needs motivation.
Are you being lazy today?

words.definition: speaking and acting in a kind and respectful way

sentences.sentence: It’s polite to say thank you after receiving help.
The waiter was very polite and professional.
Is it polite to call so late?

words.definition: not polite; likely to upset people

sentences.sentence: It was rude to interrupt while she was speaking.
He made a rude comment about my accent.
Was it rude to leave early?

words.definition: able to do something even when it is scary

sentences.sentence: She was very brave when she moved to another country alone.
Firefighters are brave people.
Was it brave to speak about the mistake?

words.definition: not comfortable with new people; quiet in groups

sentences.sentence: He is too shy to ask questions in class.
She used to be shy, but now she’s more confident.
Are you shy with new people?

words.definition: unhappy because someone has something you want

sentences.sentence: She felt jealous when her friend got the job.
He’s jealous of people who travel often.
Do you get jealous easily?

words.definition: happy because of your or someone’s good work

sentences.sentence: I’m proud of what we achieved together.
Her parents are proud because she won a prize.
Are you proud of your work?

words.definition: sad because something was not as good as you hoped

sentences.sentence: I was disappointed when the concert was cancelled.
She looked disappointed after the exam.
Were you disappointed with the result?

words.definition: feeling something is not expected

sentences.sentence: He was surprised to hear from his old teacher.
I’m surprised that you finished the project so quickly.
Were they surprised by the news?

words.definition: feeling strong dislike because something is wrong

sentences.sentence: He was angry because nobody listened to him.
Try not to get angry when things go wrong.
Are you angry with me?

words.definition: thinking about problems and feeling not calm

sentences.sentence: I’m worried about my presentation tomorrow.
She looked worried when she read the email.
Are you worried about the deadline?

words.definition: telling the truth; not lying or cheating

sentences.sentence: It’s important to be honest with your friends.
He gave an honest answer even though it was difficult.
Are you being honest with yourself?

words.definition: good at making new and interesting ideas

sentences.sentence: He’s a creative designer who always has new ideas.
You need to be creative when solving this problem.
Do you feel creative in the mornings?

words.definition: showing good judgment; practical

sentences.sentence: It’s sensible to bring a jacket in case it rains.
She made a sensible decision to save money.
Is that a sensible plan?

words.definition: caring only about yourself, not others

sentences.sentence: It was selfish of her to take all the credit.
He can be selfish sometimes but he means well.
Am I being selfish?

words.definition: happy to give time or things to others

sentences.sentence: It was generous of you to donate money.
He’s always generous with his time.
Wasn’t that a generous offer?

words.definition: doing what you should do and taking care of things

sentences.sentence: He’s responsible for opening the shop every morning.
Being responsible means you do what you promise.
Are you responsible for this task?
